item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find reliable 2024 reporting that directly identified a named Sisi family member receiving a specific asset, contract, bribe, gift, or offshore holding tied to office. The strongest 2024 material is structural: military/state economic privilege, opaque ownership, and only partial reform.","evidence":[{"title":"Egypt - United States Department of State","publisher":"U.S. Department of State","date":"2024","url":"https://2021-2025.state.gov/reports/2024-investment-climate-statements/egypt/","summary":"The report says SOEs and military-owned companies still enjoy significant advantages, including relief from regulatory requirements and, until recently, tax exemptions; some firms also hold exclusive rights over public assets and often do not publish regular financial statements. This is strong structural evidence that office-linked entities can profit through monopolies, exemptions, and opacity.","question_ids":["7B.4","7B.3"]},{"title":"Improving the business climate to revive private sector growth: OECD Economic Surveys: Egypt 2024","publisher":"OECD","date":"2024","url":"https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-egypt-2024_af900de2-en/full-report/component-8.html","summary":"OECD says military-owned firms benefit from tax and land/resource advantages, that ownership and management selection is opaque, and that public ownership structures are not transparent.
